speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Schools) whether school counsellors are or should be required to conduct psychological assessments of suicide risks of students being investigated by the Police and whether school counsellors should be required to be present when students are being interviewed by the Police on school premises.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The entire system of caring for our students, teaching them skills for emotional resilience, supporting and intervening when they have greater difficulties is developed in consultation with mental health experts, including Dr Daniel Fung, Chairman of the Medical Board of the Institute of Mental Health.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our teachers teach students the life skills to improve their emotional resilience, as I had mentioned earlier, and they are the first line of support.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The assessment is a comprehensive process that considers a range of acts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These include the student's personal circumstances, past and present challenges, medical status, coping ability and the level of support from family and friends.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The assessment also involves direct questioning of the student's intentions and plans to take his or her own life, as well as checking for prior suicide attempts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Given the dynamic psychological state of a child, suicide risk assessment is not fool-proof.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our schools monitor the student's well-being before and during the Police interview at the school.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They will continue to check on the student's well-being after the student returns home following further questioning at the Police station, as well as when the student subsequently returns to school.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Likewise, during this critical period, parents will need to give greater attention to support their child and work with the school on any follow-up steps that are necessary.
